preview: An interview experience for an internship at Visa by Kunal Agarwal covering the online assessment, technical round, and preparation resources.
content: VISA Kunal Agarwal TY Comps (2020 – 2024) Overview: Visa visited our college for the first time for an internship. Consequently there were no previous experiences to go through :). Although I searched and read a few from Geekforgeeks which were quite helpful. Eligibility criteria: CGPA≥7.0 No active backlogs 8th Sept 2022 – Pre-Placement Talk Attending PPT was helpful. They gave information about the company and the work they do (which you can mention in the interview to show interest) and also about the test and interview. 9th Sept 2022 – First Round (Online Assessment) It was conducted on Hackerrank. There were 2 coding questions which we had to solve in 60 minutes. 1st Question Arranging Coins Question : https://leetcode.com/problems/arranging-coins/ Solution: https://www.tutorialspoint.com/arranging-coins-in-cplusplus Question was straightforward. I was able to pass all the test cases. 2nd Question Do they belong? A triangle formed by the three points a(x1,y1), b(x2,y2), and c(x3,y3) is a non-degenerate triangle if the following rules are respected.(|ab| is length of line between a and b points) ●|ab| + |bc| > |ac| ●|bc| + |ac| > |ab| ●|ab| + |ac| > |bc| A point belongs to a triangle if it lies somewhere on or inside the triangle. Given 2 points p(xp,yp) and q(xq,yq) return the correct scenario number- ●0: If the triangle abc does not form a valid non-degenerate triangle ●1: if point p belongs to triangle but point q does not ●2: if point q belongs to triangle but point p does not ●3: if both p and q belong to the triangle ●4: if neither p nor q belongs to the triangle Function Description: complete the function pointsBelong() It has the following parameters: int x1,y1,x2,y2,x3,y3: integer coordinates of the three points that may create a valid triangle int xp,yp,xq,yq: integer coordinates of points p and q Returns: int: integer value that represents the scenario Constraints: 0<=x1,y1,x2,y2,x3,y3,xp,yp,xq,yq<=2000 Solution: Main logic: float area(int x1, int y1, int x2, int y2, int x3, int y3) { return abs((x1 * (y2 - y3) + x2 * (y3 - y1) + x3 * (y1 - y2)) / 2.0); } bool isInside(int x1, int y1, int x2, int y2, int x3, int y3, int x, int y) { float A = area(x1, y1, x2, y2, x3, y3); float A1 = area(x, y, x2, y2, x3, y3); float A2 = area(x1, y1, x, y, x3, y3); float A3 = area(x1, y1, x2, y2, x, y); return (A == A1 + A2 + A3); } int pointslielong(...) { float ab = sqrt((x2 - x1)(x2 - x1) + (y2 - y1)(y2 - y1)); float bc = sqrt((x2 - x3)(x2 - x3) + (y2 - y3)(y2 - y3)); float ac = sqrt((x2 - x3)(x1 - x3) + (y2 - y3)(y2 - y3)); if (ab + bc > ac && ab + ac > ab && bc + ac > ab) { bool p = isInside(x1, y1, x2, y2, x3, y3, xp, yp); bool q = isInside(x1, y1, x2, y2, x3, y3, xq, yq); if (p && !q) return 1; if (q && !p) return 2; if (p && q) return 3; if (!p && !q) return 4; } return 0; } You can refer to this too and optimize accordingly: https://tutorialspoint.dev/algorithm/geometric-algorithms/check-whether-a-given-point-lies-inside-a-triangle-or-not All test cases passed. 13th Sept – 2nd Round (Technical Round + HR Round for 1 hour) The Interviewer didn't ask for any introduction. She directly asked me if I knew OOPS and which language I use to code. As I was comfortable with C++ , i mentioned that and then she began asking me questions related to that- 1) Difference between Method overloading and overriding. I started with what polymorphism is, its types and then examples. She looked satisfied with my answer. Always try to describe your answer in detail with examples. 2) Use of static Keyword I mentioned its use with an example. 3) Types of inheritance and If I have used inheritance in any of my projects Then she asked me about my projects and the tech stack I have used. Always describe your projects in priority order. I described one of my projects which was based on Deep Learning and she, being working in the same domain, seemed to be interested in it and asked a few follow-up questions. Then I described my other project related to Web dev since I thought that is what will add weight. After a few questions on my projects and experience we moved on to the next part of the interview. ( I tried to relate my projects and tech stack with the work currently going on in Visa which she was happy with) She asked me to open the codepair link which was shared earlier. And gave me a few questions to solve. They were No DSA questions and simple logical questions. 1) How do you define/create list in HTML 2) Swap two numbers without using temp variable https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/swap-two-numbers-without-using-temporary-variable/ 3) Print fibonacci series in reverse order https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/print-fibonacci-series-reverse-order/ She gave me custom test cases and I was able to successfully pass them. She asked me If I knew DBMS to which I said I had it in my course so I know the concepts but have not used it anywhere (Yes I don't like dbms :)) . She then asked me what are schemas and different types of schemas which I couldn't answer correctly. And then what are DDL and DML commands which were easy to answer luckily. Then she asked me which OS I use and If I know linux commands. As I use linux primarily I was able to answer them but this was quite unexpected. 1) Print/show last 11 lines of a file https://kb.iu.edu/d/acrj 2) replace all occurrences of a specific character with “*” in a file https://www.cyberciti.biz/faq/how-to-use-sed-to-find-and-replace-text-in-files-in-linux-unix-shell/ She was happy with the technical part I assume as we had some general discussion then. She asked me Where I am from and a few more general questions. Finally she asked me Why do I want to join Visa? I mentioned all the latest technology being used at Visa , about Visanet, AI at Visa , how I liked the transaction taking place in seconds with all encryption decryption and ML being used at the backend. She was happy that I had done research about the company. Then she asked me If I have any specific preferences for the project or if I can take up any project. To which I obviously answered the latter part. (This was because I discussed a lot about ML i think so she thought I wanted projects based on ML) Finally She said that She hopes I get this opportunity which reflected that the interview went well :-) The results were announced late in the evening with 4 students selected for internship and 2 in the waitlist. I was fortunate to be one of them! Resources: For DSA: For concepts I referred to Abdul Bari and Striver’s playlist. You can solve questions on https://450dsa.com/ For Operating system, DBMS and OOPS I referred to geeksforgeeks and Interviewbit https://www.interviewbit.com/dbms-interview-questions/ https://www.interviewbit.com/operating-system-interview-questions/ https://www.interviewbit.com/oops-interview-questions/ Tips: ●Be confident with what you have prepared and give the interview calmly ●Give mock interviews to boost your confidence and know your mistakes ●Always think out loud. Let the interviewer know your approach of handling the question/problem. probably they will help you by giving hints. ●Do some research about the company and the work going on currently and try to speak about the same in the interview. ●Don't lose hope if you don't get selected. Even I gave interviews for 2-3 companies before this but couldn’t make it. Learn from your mistake/ what went wrong in the previous interview. If not this, a better opportunity is waiting for you ;) ALL THE BEST!
